page.layout: One printed page with running head and page number at top; one text column; a left-margin note beside the first paragraph of the chapter; a chapter heading with a title set in italic below the text; a small woodcut vignette beside the start of the chapter text; catchword at lower right.

main_text.p: pterea indefinitè etiam mouentur, quòd imaginatione careant. Imaginatio enim sensus particeps non omnibus ineft animantibus, quæ rationis expertes sunt. Altera verò, quæ deliberatiua est, soli homines præditi sunt. Hæc autē ex pluribus phantasmatis opinionem efficit. Ex quo fit, vt multæ animantes non opinantur, eo quòd eam non habeant imaginatione, quæ rationis est particeps, sed eam dutaxat, quæ sensu & cupiditate est prædita. Quoniam autem in cupiditate nullus consilio locus est, propterea ea interdum voluntatem vincit, & ad id agendum impellit, quod non bonum est: nonnunquam verò alia cupiditas aliam repellit, mouetque ho-minem, & eum maximè, qui impotens est. Ea autem mens, quæ scientijs prædita est, nihil hominem ad quicquam agedum mouet, sed stat immota, quoniam theorica est, & in sola meditatione versatur. Itaque animantiū quædam ad agendum voluntate impelluntur, vt homines: quædam cupiditate, quorum quæ imperfecta sunt, incerto motu aguntur.
main_text.head: CAP. XIX. Quisensus animantibus necessarij sunt?
main_text.p: C.12.l.3 de ani-ma.VIC QVID viuit ea anima, in qua vis alendi posita est, præditum sit, necesse est: quandoquidem crescit, vigorem ætatis habet, & senescit:

page.notes: The woodcut vignette beside the chapter opening is an ornament, not text. The left-margin note reads "C.12.l.3" on one line, "de ani-" and "ma." on the following lines; transcribed as one note. Printed oddities left as printed: "agedum" (probably for agendum), "dutaxat" (u possibly carrying a mark). The chapter title is set in italic and divides across two lines in print. The page ends with the catchword "quę" at lower right, so the last paragraph line ends at "senescit:".
